## Parent

#1

Follow the agent protocol in the parent issue (standing loop, guardrails G1–G8, evidence pack, review, merge gate).

## UI gate (mandatory — this slice ships user-visible UI)

Run the **`impeccable`** skill exactly as its SKILL.md requires: `impeccable context` first, then the matching playbook (`reference/operate.md` for app UI, `reference/new-work.md` for a new surface), and read `reference/craft-floor.md` **before any UI edit** — its craft floor is acceptance criteria, not guidance (contrast, real depth, spacing rhythm, type scale and measure, one authored motion moment, every state including hover/disabled/loading/error/empty, themed browser surfaces, product-language copy). Then run an adversarial **taste pass** (`impeccable critique` and/or the `/design-review` skill) on the rendered result and record findings and fixes in the PR. Verify in a real browser at ~360px / 768px / 1440px plus a keyboard-only pass and `prefers-reduced-motion`, with screenshots attached. Design authority is `docs/UI_DESIGN.md` + `PRODUCT.md`; `mockup/` is reference evidence for interaction and density only — never code to copy.

## What to build

Agents stop being fixtures and become durable identities — the object the whole product is organised around (D32 layer 1, D39).

- **Agent records in container SQLite** seeded from the student pack: profile, role, user-editable instructions, capability list, default provider/model (placeholder values until the providers slice), private folder `agent://<id>/`, private memory store (publication rules arrive in the memory slice), settings surface, and task history.
- **Six direct Agent chats** (PRD §19 AC3), each backed by a real conversation and reachable from the sidebar **Agents** section.
- **One identity everywhere** (D39): one profile, one direct chat, one private memory, one settings surface per Agent — never a duplicate identity per Operation. Chats reference the same `agent_id`.
- **Private folder isolation**: an Agent reads/writes its own `agent://<id>/` folder and the shared workspace per its permissions; another Agent's private folder is not readable by it.
- **Agent settings surface** using the same command schemas onboarding and settings will use (D16): role (read-only, from pack), user instructions (editable), memory link, default provider/model, tool defaults — each with recommended default, current value, and reset-to-default.
- **Chat header identity**: avatar, name, role, and presence placeholder (session states become real in the next slice).

## Decisions and specs

- PRD §5 (Agent definitions), §4.2 (Agent chat), §19 AC3/AC4; D32 (persistent identity), D39 (one identity, scoped assignments), D18/D28 (profile content comes from the pack), D16 (settings commands/schemas), E12 (`workspace_id` scoping), `docs/UI_DESIGN.md` S3, S9 Agents category, §5 avatars.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] All six Agents from the pack are available as direct chats with persistent history across restart (AC3).
- [ ] An Agent's stored profile matches the pack it was pinned to; editing user instructions persists and does not rewrite pack files.
- [ ] Cross-Agent private-folder access is denied and the denial is tested (not just prevented in the UI).
- [ ] A test asserts no second identity is created for an Agent inside an Operation (one `agent_id` referenced everywhere).
- [ ] Profile edits, default model, and tool defaults survive a runtime restart (AC16 partially — files and identity persist).
- [ ] Settings rows show recommended default, current value, and reset-to-default; reset actually restores the pack/policy default.
- [ ] Regression budget: E2E login→chat→stream→replay still green; pack validation tests still green.

## Blocked by

- #10
- #11


## Open-source leverage (recorded 2026-09-18)

- **Pattern:** Letta (https://docs.letta.com/ — read the Agents → Memory docs) for memory-block scoping, provenance, and agents-as-durable-identities vocabulary. Implementation stays custom on SQLite per D37/D39 — copy semantics, not schema.
- **Embed:** nothing new — reuse the S02 contracts package.
